Interesting. This is a PE32+ (x86-64) console executable. It has 19 sections, including several unusually-named sections (/4, /19, /31, etc.) which look like sections merged from static libraries (these names appear when linking static libs - e.g. mingw static linking of libmingw32 etc.). Actually section names like "/4", "/19" are from COFF long-section-name handling — when a section name is longer than 8 chars, the name field contains "/<offset>" pointing into the string table. Without the string table loaded, they appear as /4, /19, etc. These are typical of MinGW-linked binaries with sections like .text$_..., .rdata$.refptr etc.? Hmm, actually those names with slashes appear in PE files linked by MinGW when sections come from archive members.

Imports are interesting:
- CreateProcessA, GetThreadContext, SetThreadContext, ResumeThread, VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, VirtualFreeEx — this is the classic combo for **process hollowing** (create suspended process, unmap/alloc, write payload, set context, resume).
- GetModuleHandleA, GetProcAddress — possibly manual API resolution.
- SetUnhandledExceptionFilter, signal — maybe anti-debug or just CRT.

TLS callbacks present.
